featured_reviews.review_text:
To,
The Management,
Sanjeevni Hospital, Andheri East

Subject: Serious Concerns Regarding Hospital Facilities, Staff Management & Patient Care

I am writing this feedback with deep disappointment regarding the overall experience and facilities provided during our patient’s admission for knee replacement surgery at your hospital.

There appears to be only 1 sister/nurse and 1 housekeeping staff managing 3 floors. In case of emergencies, even after ringing the bell repeatedly, the staff arrives extremely late — sometimes after nearly an hour. In a medical emergency, such delays can become life-threatening. The management seriously needs to address this issue immediately and appoint more staff for proper patient care and safety.

The cleanliness and maintenance standards of the hospital are also extremely poor. Rooms and patient areas were not cleaned properly, and hygiene was highly disappointing.

Food service was another major concern:
- Morning breakfast was either delayed or sometimes not provided at all.

Update: I’ve experienced both private consultation and general OPD at Holy Spirit Hospital, and overall, it has been a bad experience.

The campus itself is beautiful and well maintained. Online appointment booking is smooth, while offline booking starts at 7:30 am and doctors typically begin consultations from around 8:30 am.

The private consultation experience (ENT, in my case) was genuinely good. The doctor gave adequate time, listened patiently, and the interaction felt reassuring and professional. However, this comes at a cost, as the visit including diagnostics ended up in the range of ₹3,000–4,000.

The general OPD experience was very bad. The charges are in the range of ₹400-700.

Earlier I had positive experiences with  Gastroenterology and Surgery. I was very much impressed with the surgeon, but his opinion was outrightly dismissed by 3 other senior surgeons and physicians. I realised he kept focussing on a know problem which wasn't connected to my pain.  Gastroenterologist doesn't do any physical examination to understand the location of pain or confirm hemorrhoids. Seems, he only checks you during pricey colonoscopy and endoscopy procedures.

My experience with General Medicine and Urology OPD was disappointing. In these departments, the main doctor and an assistant doctor sit at the same small table and consult two different patients simultaneously.

In General Medicine OPD, there were up to four patients along with their attendants inside the same room at once—one with the main doctor, one with the assistant, one waiting behind the doctor, and another at the entrance being triaged for blood pressure and weight. That easily translates to 8–10 people in a single consultation room. There is no space for discussion, questions, nuance, or privacy. The doctor barely had time for eye contact, let alone a detailed conversation or examination.

In the Urology OPD, I could speak to the actual doctor only after the assistant doctor felt I was not convinced. While I do not question the competence of junior doctors, as a patient it feels unfair when you do not get adequate time with the consultant you booked.

I guess this is the truth of INR 400-700 consultations. I sincerely hope the PRO and hospital administration take note of these inconsistencies, especially given Holy Spirit’s reputation as an esteemed institution.

We have carefully read your review and the multiple updates you have made over time. While we respect your right to share experiences, repeated edits with selective interpretations create confusion rather than clarity for the public.

Holy Spirit Hospital has been serving the community for over 57 years with a clear mission:
➡️ to provide ethical, quality medical care at affordable costs, especially for patients who are financially constrained.

It is important to place a few facts on record for transparency:

1️⃣ General OPD vs Private Consultation

Holy Spirit Hospital deliberately maintains low-cost General OPD consultations (₹400–₹700) so that patients from all economic backgrounds can access senior medical care. This is a conscious, charitable decision — not a compromise in quality.

Some consultants also run private OPD sessions at charges decided by them, purely for convenience and extended consultation time.
➡️ The hospital does not interfere in private OPD fees.

Comparing a low-cost charitable OPD with a private consultation model is not an apples-to-apples comparison.

2️⃣ Consultation Cost with Diagnostics

Your claim of ₹3,000–₹4,000 includes diagnostic investigations.
Any investigation—whether blood tests, imaging, or endoscopy—is:

Done only if clinically required

Clearly chargeable, as per standard medical practice anywhere in the world

This is not unique to Holy Spirit Hospital.

3️⃣ Regarding Junior Doctors

The doctors you refer to as “assistants” are not casual or unqualified staff.
They are:

Postgraduate doctors (MD/MS/DNB)

Having completed 3 years of rigorous specialty training

Working under direct supervision of senior consultants with 25–35+ years of experience

They are competent, qualified, and trained to evaluate patients thoroughly.
If a patient requests direct interaction with the senior consultant, that is always accommodated.

4️⃣ Multiple Patients in OPD Rooms

General OPD caters to high patient volumes, precisely because of its affordability. This allows thousands of patients daily—many of whom cannot afford private healthcare—to receive treatment from experienced specialists.

This model is transparent, intentional, and patient-centric, not neglectful.

5️⃣ Allegation of Doctors “Pushing Procedures”

Any invasive procedure such as endoscopy or colonoscopy is recommended only after clinical assessment, based on medical guidelines—not for revenue generation. Suggesting otherwise without evidence is a serious misrepresentation of ethical medical practice.

6️⃣ Repeated Updates to the Same Review

Repeatedly modifying the same review with escalating commentary, despite explanations, raises concerns about intent.
Constructive feedback is always welcome; repeated public reinterpretation without engagement does not help patients or institutions improve.

You have shared your Hospital ID, and we reiterate our request:
➡️ Please meet our PRO or Medical Administration so this can be discussed clinically and factually, rather than through ongoing public speculation.

Holy Spirit Hospital remains committed to:

Ethical medicine

Affordable care

Training future specialists

Serving patients who otherwise would have no access to quality healthcare

We stand by our doctors, our systems, and our mission.

Holy Spirit Hospital, Andheri East

featured_reviews.name: Naseem Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Outside India currently and had my wife visit her clinic as she is currently pregnant. She had the most disturbing experience speaking with Dr. Vaishali Ghiya, the primary obstetrician at Carewel.

We had first visited Carewel 3 years ago for our first child. For the delivery, however, I had to take my wife to the hospital at 3 AM and there was no transport available. So we decided to go to the second hospital that we had registered in which was closer to where we live.

My wife had the Carewel file from her previous pregnancy which she carried  with her yesterday while visiting Carewel hospital. Dr Vaishali Ghiya was clearly upset that we chose to go to the second hospital on our list last time.

She made so many nasty comments that my wife almost cried. It's a shame that someone so educated has such a vile tongue. Some of the comments that she made are:

1. You guys are so poor. Maybe you cannot afford treatment here.
2. You should go to a government hospital
3. I will charge Rs 1500 to give an IV. Can you afford that? Should I start the treatment?
4. Why did you come here now? Why didn’t you go to the second hospital? Did something go wrong there?
5. Why are you coming when you are so far along?
6. There are two medicines, one for 1800, one for 2400 which one can you afford?

My wife and MIL, being kind and reserved, took these comments in silence. But is this any way for a doctor to talk to the patients? What kind of an example does it set for those working under her? Will nurses and wardboys also have the same attitude when a patient is admitted?

For perspective, my wife and I have a combined income of over 36LPA and, if we wanted, we could go to the most expensive hospital in Mumbai. We are shocked to see such an attitude from a doctor that treats women when they are at their most vulnerable. Honestly, I think we dodged a bullet here.

The irony is that my modestly dressed wife and I could pay for 12 deliveries at Carewel and still have money left over from our monthly income.

featured_reviews.name: Siddharth Shivram
featured_reviews.review_text:
Based on my experience on 10th May 2021:

Since this is a new centre for vaccination opened last Friday by the BMC, there is not much clarity/information available online. This centre is currently open for 18-44 age group, and primarily Covaxin (subject to availability). There is not much clarity about walk-ins, better to call and confirm as they were only accepting appointments via CoWIN when I visited. Location specified on Google Maps is accurate.

An extremely well-maintained, organized vaccination centre with professional service by the officials. There are 3-4 levels of screenings and procedures before you get vaccinated, which is managed brilliantly. Prefer a morning slot if possible, reach the centre by 8:30am. They allow entry in an orderly manner at sharp 9am if everything goes well.

First level: General health details. Please provide accurate answers to the questions about any health conditions, symptoms, etc.

Second level: This is where you receive your token/card from BMC with all your details, verified with your appointment online. They will also specify booth/token number. After this, proceed to the waiting zone, which has an LED indicator to show the current token ongoing.

Third level: Once your token number is displayed, proceed to your booth (there are 2 booths which function simultaneously) and wait for the previous person to vacate. Get vaccinated, follow all the necessary instructions specified by the vaccinating doctor, and proceed towards the observation zone.

Fourth level: Wait patiently for 30 minutes. Please do not insist to leave any earlier, just to make sure there are no side effects. Once your 30-minute cooldown is complete, you can show your token/card and collect your vaccination certificate.

The entire process, takes just about 30-40 minutes, thanks to the dedicated staff (this was specifically for the morning slot 9-11am, your experience may vary depending on the time of the day).
Kindly co-operate with the officials, and please be patient, they are way more stressed than us, we need to go through this process just once per dose. Overall, it was totally worth 40 minutes of my travel to this centre.

I had a very bad experience at SevenHills Hospital.

When we admitted our patient, he was able to walk into the hospital on his own. He was admitted to the emergency ward under Dr. Deepesh Makhijani on Saturday. However, after admission, Dr. Makhijani never came to see the patient even once. Later, we were informed that he had gone on official leave without informing the patient’s relatives.

After that, Dr. Dinesh Giri took over the case. He explained the patient’s condition to us on Monday and Tuesday. But on Wednesday morning, he did not visit the patient. He only came in the evening and then told us that he did not know how many hours the patient would survive. We were not properly informed when the ventilator was removed, and CPR was given without clear communication with the family.

The nursing staff were also very careless. Medicines were not administered properly, and the patient developed swelling and infections in his hands. Most of the time, only RMOs or junior doctors (interns) were attending to the patient. Senior doctors did not seem to give proper attention or care.

Unfortunately, we lost our patient. We strongly feel that there was negligence from Dr. Dinesh Giri, Dr. Vilaya, and Dr. Deepesh Makhijani.

Based on our experience, I would not recommend this hospital to others.

In my opinion, no patient admitted under government schemes like MCGM or MJPJY receives proper care in this hospital. If your patient is shifted to the ICU under these schemes, there is very little hope of recovery. It feels like the hospital is only focused on money. They seem more concerned about payments than about saving patients’ lives.

Based on my experience, this hospital operates like a money-making business rather than a place that genuinely cares for patients.
